messages.subject: Seemingly Unrelated Regressions
parts:
Dear Stan Users Group,

This is almost certainly a very simple mistake on my part, but it has me stumped. Any help greatly appreciated.

I am trying to fit a seemingly unrelated regressions model in Stan. I note the previous discussion - at  https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups#!searchin/stan-users/Seemingly$20unrelated$20regression/stan-users/e1Uw2t6al8k/ak5O4AYoLMgJ  - to which my question is really a continuation.

The model I am trying to fit -- to start with, what I really want to do is more complex -- is given as:

data {
                 int <lower=1> N_obs;
                 real <lower=2006, upper=2010> year;
                 vector[2] y[N_obs];
                    }
                           
            parameters {
                        real <lower=0> sigma[2];
                        real <lower=-1, upper=1> rho;
                        real <lower=0> mu[2];
                        vector [2] beta ;
                        }
             
            transformed parameters{
                cov_matrix[2] Sigma;
                Sigma[1,1] <- square(sigma[1]);
                Sigma[2,2] <- square(sigma[2]);
                Sigma[1,2] <- rho;
                Sigma[2,1] <- rho;
                       }
                      
            model {
               
                    beta ~ normal(0, 10);
                    for(n in 1:N_obs){
                        y[n] ~ multi_normal(year[n]*beta, Sigma) ;
                    }
                       
                }
            }

When I try to run this model I get an indexing error: My data has the structure as follows:

N_obs <- 355

year -- a vector of length 355, containing the year of the observation

str(y) in R gives:

> str(y)
 num [1:355, 1:2] 3.07e+08 4.72e+07 8.45e+07 1.50e+09 1.97e+08 ...
 - attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
  ..$ : NULL
  ..$ : chr [1:2] "core" "prog"
>

Where am I going wrong? Some further information is  given below.

Lindsay




To give just a bit more information, in case the above is not sufficient, the error message in full reads:

Actually, I think I solved my problem (which turned out to be something I shouldn't really be bothering the Stan list with). I'm not great at debugging. Apologies. Here is code that I think works for anyone who has a similar problem:

data {
                 int <lower=1> N_obs;
                 real <lower=2006, upper=2010> year[N_obs];

vector[2] y[N_obs];
                    }
                           
            parameters {
                        real <lower=0> sigma[2];
                        real <lower=-1, upper=1> rho;

vector [2] beta ;
                        }
             
            transformed parameters{
                cov_matrix[2] Sigma;
                Sigma[1,1] <- square(sigma[1]);
                Sigma[2,2] <- square(sigma[2]);
                Sigma[1,2] <- rho;
                Sigma[2,1] <- rho;
                       }
                      
            model {
                    beta ~ normal(0, 10);
                    for(n in 1:N_obs){
                        y[n] ~ multi_normal(year[n]*beta, Sigma);
                    }

On Tuesday, April 15, 2014 11:01:59 AM UTC-4, Lindsay wrote:
            transformed parameters{
                cov_matrix[2] Sigma;
                Sigma[1,1] <- square(sigma[1]);
                Sigma[2,2] <- square(sigma[2]);
                Sigma[1,2] <- rho;
                Sigma[2,1] <- rho;
                       }

For a covariance matrix, you want

Sigma[1,2] <- rho* sigma[1] * sigma[2];
Sigma[2,1] <- Sigma[1,2];

Ben
